item.title: Human-centric innovation in the age of interactive technologies
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Sestino, Luiss Guido Carli University

Luigi Nasta, John Cabot University

Vitor Lima, ESCP Madrid

Russell W. Belk, Schulich Business School

This special issue bridges innovation management and consumer behavior by examining how digital technologies influence emotional engagement and social connection. It explores whether anthropomorphic technologies like chatbots and AI assistants create authentic human connections or risk fostering detachment, and how emotional and social factors shape technology adoption across healthcare, tourism, customer service, and business contexts.

The collection seeks research on designing human-centric innovations that maintain emotional depth, foster trust, and enable long-term value creation. It addresses ethical considerations, the role of digital identity and extended self, and organizational strategies for implementing emotionally intelligent technologies while preserving non-verbal communication and authentic interaction.

Appel publié par European Journal of Innovation Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Design principles for anthropomorphic digital tools
  • Digitalization and emotional engagement in tourism
  • Emotional seeking behavior in consumers
  • Digital technologies and emotional authenticity
  • Extended self and digital features
  • Ethical considerations in emotionally intelligent technologies
  • Emotional intelligence in digital marketing
  • AI, VR, and human emotion
  • Emotional and social barriers to digital innovation adoption
  • Human-centric innovation design
  • Emotional drivers of AI and digital service innovation acceptance
  • Organizational implications of emotionally intelligent digital innovations
  • Emotional trust and legitimacy in digital innovation ecosystems
  • Case studies in maintaining emotional engagement across sectors

  • January 11, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submissions

item.title: Customer development in digital innovation and entrepreneurship
item.content:encoded:
Marcin Waldemar Staniewski, VIZJA University

Ricardo Costa-Climent, Universitat de València

Rohail Hassan, Universiti Utara Malaysia

This special issue explores the intersection of customer development, digital innovation, and entrepreneurship. The call addresses how digital technologies enable ventures to align business ideas with market demands and consumer preferences. Customer development emerged as a critical approach when traditional product development methods failed in market penetration.

Digital tools have made idea validation and market exploration more accessible to entrepreneurs. Advanced technologies such as generative AI, digital twins, and digital nudging accelerate customer validation cycles and refine product offerings. The synergy between innovation processes, technology, and customer development is essential for entrepreneurial success through precise understanding of consumer needs.

The issue invites submissions addressing sustainable innovation, circular entrepreneurship, open innovation ecosystems, lean start-up approaches, and AI-driven business models. It seeks research on how digital platforms and emerging technologies support entrepreneurial ventures in developing products that meet market demands.
